learning_outcomes.text: Calculate the integrity of cracked industrial components under the action of service mechanical loads.
Calculate the life of industrial components under fatigue loads and combinations of static load/corrosive environment, and also to assess the influence of affecting factors.
Predict the behavior of materials in creep, oxidation, and hot corrosion situations, and select the most suitable materials for each particular case.
Foresee the behavior of materials in friction/wear situations and select the most suitable materials for each particular case.
Define the appropriate surface modification technology to withstand different service actions.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental mechanical properties: Tensile, compression and bending tests. Behavior of metallic alloys, ceramics and plastic materials. Tests on notched specimens.
Toughness: Definition of impact toughness. Charpy tests. Ductile-brittle transition curve and transition temperature. Factors influencing brittleness. Other tests for measuring toughness.
Micromechanisms of fracture: Microstructure. Hardening mechanisms. Ductile, brittle and intergranular fracture. Microstructural modifications for increasing material toughness.
Linear elastic fracture mechanics: Energy criterion for fracture. Stress state ahead of a crack. Stress intensity factor. Fracture toughness. Plane stress versus plane strain.
Elastoplastic fracture mechanics: CTOD and J integral. Fracture criteria. Experimental determination of material toughness. Limitations of elastoplastic fracture mechanics.
Fatigue: Load cycles. Justifying mechanisms of cracking in fatigue. Descriptive laws. Fatigue limit. Standardized tests. Threshold value and fatigue crack growth rate. Calculation of fatigue lives.
Environmentally assisted fracture: Justifying mechanisms. Descriptive laws. Standardized tests. Threshold value and environmentally assisted crack growth rate. Calculation of service lives.
Creep: Evolution of deformation as a function of time. Descriptive laws of creep. Stress relaxation at high temperature. Creep deformation mechanisms. Deformation maps.
Oxidation and hot corrosion. Justifying mechanisms of these processes. Reaction kinetics and behavior laws. Development of high-temperature resistant materials. Hot corrosion.

Wet corrosion. Thermodynamics and kinetics of corrosive processes. Electrode potentials and galvanic cells. Justifying mechanisms. Passivation. Corrosion morphologies. Methods for controlling corrosive processes. Electrochemical protection.
Friction and wear of materials. Surface contact. Adhesive, abrasive, and fatigue wear. Tests.
Surface protection technologies. Surface treatments. Coatings and application methods. Comparison of available processes.
assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation, if all minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as 0.1*PLs + 0.1*EP1 + 0.1*EP2 + 0.04*EO1 + 0.04*EO2 + 0.62*EF. A minimum of 4 points out of 10 in the Final Exam (EF) is mandatory, with at least 30% in both the exercise and theoretical parts of the EF. A minimum overall score of 5 out of 10 is required to pass. For extraordinary evaluation, the Final Exam (EF) is weighted at 62%, and previous scores from PLs, EP1, EP2, EO1-PL13, and EO2-TG are carried over. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is 0.05*PLs + 0.025*EO1 + 0.025*EO2 + 0.9*EF, with a minimum of 4.5 points out of 10 in the EF and at least 30% in all its parts. In all cases, failure to meet minimums or overall passing grade results in a maximum grade of 4.0. Grades for PLs, EP1, EP2, EO1-PL1 and EO2-TG are not carried over to the next academic year if the subject is not passed.
